about: Entries for CPUIDs the article has no row for, each fact with the page it came from. import.py appends them after the article's and refuses one whose CPUID the article has: the article's own row is kept. A model's codes are ARK's, in ark-sspec.json, placed by enrich.py. A stepping no source ties to the CPUID is left empty, not guessed.

evidence.quote: 06_7AH: stepping 8, Gemini Lake, CPUID 706A8 — none for 706A0.

entries.note: coreboot names 706A0 Gemini Lake A0. Intel's list has no row for it, its microcode notes name 06-7a-01 (B0) and 06-7a-08 (R0) only, and its one public microcode is dated 2017-07-12, months before Gemini Lake's launch. No models.

evidence.quote: 06_7EH: stepping 5, Ice Lake U/Y, CPUID 706E5 — none for 706E0.

entries.note: Model 0x7E is Ice Lake (the kernel). Intel's list of processors by CPUID has only 706E5 for it, its microcode notes only 06-7e-05 (D1), and coreboot names no 0x706E stepping, so 706E0 has no stepping written and no models.

entries.note: Model 0x7E is Ice Lake (the kernel). Intel's list of processors by CPUID has only 706E5 for it, its microcode notes only 06-7e-05 (D1), and coreboot names no 0x706E stepping, so 706E1 has no stepping written and no models; its one public microcode is one update with 706E2.

evidence.quote: Products formerly Knights Mill: Xeon Phi 7235, 7285, 7295 (7255: SKU 128693); Vertical Segment: Server

entries.note: Model 0x85 is Knights Mill (the kernel); the collection's one microcode for it is 80650. ARK gives the 7235, 7285 and 7295 codes at stepping A0, which no source ties to stepping ID 0, so no stepping is written; the 7255 has no ordering tab. Intel's list of processors by CPUID has no 06_85H row.
coreboot names 806C0 Tiger Lake A0; Intel's list has no row for it, and its one public microcode is dated 2020-04-02, before Tiger Lake's launch. No models.
coreboot names 806D0 Tiger Lake P0; Intel's list has only 806D1 (R0) for 06_8DH, and the microcode notes name no 06-8d-00. No models.

Intel's microcode notes list 06-8e-0d as Whiskey Lake U V0, as they do 806EC; Intel's list of processors by CPUID has no 806ED and the collection no microcode for it. ARK's V0 models are under 806EC, so none is listed here.
Sapphire Rapids' 806F3; Intel's list of processors by CPUID has no row for it, and no model on ARK gives its stepping. No models.
Sapphire Rapids' 806F4; Intel's list of processors by CPUID has no row for it, and no model on ARK gives its stepping. No models.

06_8FH | 5, 6, 8 | Sapphire Rapids (Golden Cove) | Intel Xeon CPU Max Series processors (High Bandwidth Memory HBM) | Server | 806F8
Each model's ARK ordering tab gives its code at E5, S3 (4th Gen Xeon Scalable, Xeon W-2400/2500/3400/3500) or B3 (Xeon CPU Max) — ark-sspec.json
Component Identification via Capability Registers: XCC E-5/E-4 Server, 1S 806F8/806F7; MCC S-3/S-2 Server, 1S 806F8/806F7; HBM B-3 Server, 1S 806F8

entries.note: The models are those whose ARK ordering tab gives an E5, S3 or B3 code. Left out: Xeon Gold 5403N, Xeon Gold 5423N, Xeon Gold 5433N, Xeon Gold 6403N, Xeon Gold 6423N, Xeon Gold 6433N, Xeon Gold 6433NE, Xeon Gold 6443N — ARK gives them L0 or U1 and the code name "Sapphire Rapids Edge Enhanced" (read for the 6403N and 5423N); neither Intel's microcode notes, its list of processors by CPUID nor the 4th Gen Xeon Scalable Specification Update (772415-016, which ties XCC E-5/E-4, MCC S-3/S-2 and HBM B-3 to 806F8/806F7) names those steppings. Their codes are kept in ark-sspec.json.

evidence.quote: 06_9AH | 4 | CPUID.0x7.EDX[15] =0 | Arizona Beach (Gracemont) | Intel Atom Processors | Embedded | 906A4 | 0xc
Product Collection: Intel Atom® Processor C Series; Code Name: Products formerly Arizona Beach; Vertical Segment: Embedded (C1100 SKU 229204, C1110 229206, C1130 229205)

entries.note: Arizona Beach shares 906A4 with Alder Lake U; only the hybrid bit (CPUID.0x7.EDX[15]: 0 here, 1 for Alder Lake U) and the microcode's platform (0x40) tell them apart. ARK has no ordering tab for the three models, so no S-SPEC is known.

evidence.quote: The one row for 06_B6H is stepping 4, CPUID B0664 — none for B0660.
cpuB0664_plat01_ver00000030_2025-05-29_PRD_E618875A.bin — the one microcode of model 0xB6; none for B0660.

entries.note: The kernel names model 0xB6 Grand Ridge whatever its stepping. No source names a model sold as B0660: Intel's list of processors by CPUID, ARK's Grand Ridge models and the public microcode collections know only B0664. So the entry has no models, and none of B0664's are moved here.

evidence.quote: 06_B6H | 4 | … | Grand Ridge (Crestmont) | Intel® Atom® Processors P6000 series | Server | B0664 | 0x36
Products formerly Grand Ridge: Atom P6952-3, P6942-3, P6962-3, P6962-5, P6942-5, P6922-3
Product Collection: Intel Atom® Processor P Series; Code Name: Products formerly Grand Ridge; Vertical Segment: Server

entries.note: Intel's list of processors by CPUID gives B0664 (model 0xB6, stepping ID 4) as Grand Ridge, Atom P6000 series. Every Grand Ridge code on ARK is stepping B0, but no Intel page loaded names the stepping of ID 4, so the entry has none. Intel's Linux microcode repository has no 06-b6-04 file (checked 2026-11-07).

evidence.quote: #define INTEL_RAPTORLAKE		IFM(6, 0xB7) /* Raptor Cove / Enhanced Gracemont */
06_B7H rows: stepping 1, B0671 (Raptor Lake S; Catlow) — none for B0670.
cpuB0670_plat02_ver0000000E_2022-02-20_PRD_0A83935A.bin — revision 0x0E, platform 0x02, no extended signature table.

entries.note: coreboot names B0670 Raptor Lake A0; the kernel names model 0xB7 Raptor Lake. No source names a model sold as B0670: Intel's list of processors by CPUID has only B0671 for 06_B7H, and the one public microcode for B0670 (revision 0x0E) is dated 2022-02-20, months before Raptor Lake's launch. So the entry has no models.

evidence.quote: | BTL-S816       | B0       | 06-b7-04/36 |          | 00000137 | Intel Core Series 2 Processors with P-cores

entries.note: Intel's microcode notes name 06-b7-04 BTL-S816, stepping B0, one update with B0671 and D0670. ARK lists Bartlett Lake models on B0 (Core 7 251E SRQDU, 251TE SRQAX, Core 5 221E SRQDV, 211E SRQER), but B0 is B0671's name too and no Intel document says which of the two CPUIDs they report, so none is listed. Intel's list of processors by CPUID has no B0674.

evidence.quote: 06_BAH | 2,3,8 | … | Raptor Lake P / H / U Refresh | … | Mobile | B06A2, B06A3, B06A8

entries.note: Intel's list of processors by CPUID gives B06A8 with B06A2 (J0) and B06A3 (Q0) as Raptor Lake P/H/U Refresh; one microcode serves all three. No Intel document names its stepping — the 13th/14th gen datasheet (743844-015) and specification update (740518-032) list only B06A2 and B06A3 — so no model is listed.

evidence.quote: 06_BDH: stepping 1, Lunar Lake, Core Ultra 5, 7, 9, Mobile, CPUID B06D1 — none for B06D0.
cpuB06D0_plat80_ver0000001A_2024-06-10_PRD_D7BD1337.bin — revision 0x1A, platform 0x80, no extended signature table.

entries.note: Lunar Lake's stepping ID 0. No source names a model sold as B06D0: Intel's list of processors by CPUID has only B06D1 for 06_BDH, and its one public microcode (0x1A) is dated 2024-06-10, before Lunar Lake's launch. coreboot calls it A0, but also calls B06D1 "A0_2" where Intel's notes call it B0, so no stepping is written.

evidence.quote: Each model's ARK ordering tab lists its codes at stepping H0 (ark-sspec.json); Code Name "Products formerly Raptor Lake", Vertical Segment "Desktop" (i3-13100, i3-14100, Processor 300), "Embedded" (i3-13100E)

entries.note: The article has no row for B06F5. Intel's microcode notes call 06-bf-05 RPL-S H0 since 2024 (earlier releases called it ADL C0); coreboot names 0xb06f5 Raptor Lake H0. The models are those whose ARK ordering tab gives an H0 code among the 13th/14th gen 4-core and 2-core desktop and embedded parts; the i5-13400/14400 (B0, C0) and Xeon E-2400 (B0) have none. Alder Lake's H0 is another CPUID, 90675.
